title: Return value of right-sequenced timed computations
statement: Model a computation that tracks its running time as a pair consisting of a return value and an accumulated time cost drawn from a type $T$ equipped with an addition. Given such a computation $x$, with return value in a type $\alpha$, and a thunk $y$ producing a second such computation with return value in a type $\beta$, the right-sequencing of $x$ and $y$ — which runs $x$, then $y()$, combines their time costs, and discards the value of $x$ — has return value equal to that of $y()$.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a timed computation with value in $\alpha$
$y$ is a thunk producing a timed computation with value in $\beta$
replaced: The right-sequencing of $x$ and $y$ returns the value returned by $y\,()$.
